boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Carolina rituals, annual gatherings and campus customs.

cards.title: Start Classes With First Sip
cards.subtitle: Old Well, McCorkle Place
cards.notes: On the first day of classes, visit the Old Well and take part in First Sip if the fountain is operating; use the accessible approach and respect the queue.
cards.short_summary: A first-day water ritual connected with luck and the hope of a perfect GPA.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC identifies First Sip as the tradition of students drinking Old Well water for good luck and a perfect GPA on the first day of classes.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; fountain availability and campus conditions can change.

cards.title: Find the Tree That “Holds Up” Carolina
cards.subtitle: Davie Poplar, McCorkle Place
cards.notes: Pause at Davie Poplar to learn the campus legend linking the tree’s fate to the University; view it from established paths and do not touch or climb it.
cards.short_summary: A centuries-old campus myth attached to Carolina’s historic tulip poplar.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC documents the legend that the University will fall if Davie Poplar falls, while noting the myth’s origin is unknown.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor historic tree in McCorkle Place; keep off protected landscaping.

cards.title: Listen for the Student Bell Ringers
cards.subtitle: Morehead-Patterson Bell Tower
cards.notes: Listen from public campus space on a football game day or special occasion, when student master bell ringers operate the Bell Tower.
cards.short_summary: Students carry forward a bell-ringing tradition at Carolina’s signature tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says student master bell ringers oversee Bell Tower operations and ring its bells on football game days and other special occasions.
cards.access_notes: Ringing is event-dependent; do not seek access to the tower’s controlled interior.

cards.title: Plan for the Senior Bell Tower Climb
cards.subtitle: Morehead-Patterson Bell Tower
cards.notes: Eligible graduating Tar Heels can watch for official Senior Week details for this Bell Tower climb; do not attempt entry outside authorized access.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-season opportunity to climb one of Carolina’s defining landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that graduating Tar Heels have the opportunity to participate in the Senior Bell Tower Climb.
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to official opportunities; follow Alumni Association instructions.

cards.title: Look for the Live Rameses
cards.subtitle: Carolina athletic events
cards.notes: At an authorized athletics event, look for Rameses and enjoy the live-mascot tradition from the audience area; follow staff instructions around the animal.
cards.short_summary: Carolina’s live ram mascot tradition began at a 1924 football game.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that the live animal Rameses mascot began attending Carolina football games in 1924.
cards.access_notes: Appearances are event-dependent and may require an event ticket.

cards.title: Spot the Costumed Rameses
cards.subtitle: Carolina athletic events
cards.notes: Watch for the costumed Rameses at a Carolina event and enjoy from public spectator space; mascot appearances vary by sport and schedule.
cards.short_summary: A student-carried mascot role that began with the 1987–88 basketball season.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says the costumed Rameses tradition began when Eric Chilton first wore the costume for the 1987–88 basketball season and continues today.
cards.access_notes: Appearances are event-dependent and venue admission rules may apply.

cards.title: Make Space for Arts Everywhere Day
cards.subtitle: UNC-Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Check the annual program and join an activity that fits your interests, from singing and dancing to painting; follow each host’s participation guidance.
cards.short_summary: A campuswide annual arts celebration held since 2017.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that Tar Heels have celebrated the annual Arts Everywhere Day tradition since 2017, with activities including singing, dancing and painting.
cards.access_notes: Annual programming, locations and any registration requirements vary.

cards.title: Join the Colors at Holi Moli
cards.subtitle: UNC-Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Attend through the official event organizers, wear clothes suitable for color powder and follow on-site guidance about accessibility, cleanup and participation.
cards.short_summary: A yearly campus celebration of Holi that brings students and the local community together.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says Holi Moli has been a yearly Carolina tradition since 2008 and connects campus with the local community.
cards.access_notes: Annual event details and participation instructions are set by the organizers.

cards.title: Mark Carolina’s University Day
cards.subtitle: Memorial Hall, UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Watch for the annual Oct. 12 ceremony and attend only with current event information; it commemorates Old East’s cornerstone and honors members of the Carolina community.
cards.short_summary: Carolina’s annual ceremony marking the founding-era cornerstone of Old East.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that University Day marks the Oct. 12, 1793 laying of Old East’s cornerstone, was first celebrated in 1877 and includes annual recognition of distinguished alumni.
cards.access_notes: The annual ceremony’s venue, entry policies and schedule should be confirmed on the current event page.

cards.title: Sing “Hark the Sound”
cards.subtitle: University programs and athletic events
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before an event, then join in when invited; Carolina identifies it as a song sung at University programs and sporting events.
cards.short_summary: The alma mater that closes many Carolina gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s family handbook identifies “Hark the Sound” as the alma mater and says it is sung at University programs and sporting events.
cards.source_title: Carolina Family Handbook | UNC New Student and Family Programs
cards.access_notes: Occurs in event contexts; attendance and accessibility conditions depend on the hosting program.

warnings: Several traditions are event- or eligibility-dependent; confirm current University scheduling and access guidance before going.
